John

Hi Vivek
Actually it worked fine although I will sort it in decending order. 

The problem was that I use RStudio. which I definately like but once in a long while (maybe one a year?) it goes wonky and that's what it did yesterday.  Just after I replied to us and was ready to shut down for the day I did copy and paste and much to my surprise the paste had the copied text plus about 3 characters from an earlier copy and paste.  A reboot of the computer and reloading of RStudio solved the problem.  Apparently it was not doing the sort you had specified properly.

 For some reason I thought that I had to do the sort with ggplot(), though I cannot remember why I thought that.

Thanks very much for the help.
John
P.S. I hope the baby is sleeping well.

parts:
You can accomplish the same without the cast/melt route.

ggplot(mdat, aes(reorder(town, -hours, function(x)x[1]), hours, colour = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_flip()

The idea is to reorder town based on the first element of hours, which will be the hours corresponding to coach1836. I did a quick check and the plot I get resembles the one that Vivek had in his html document.
